body:
I disagree. The cases where the signal needs to be implemented in the core are those where we needs to interject a callback or the property is changed in the class's hard-coded behavior, or the class's property needs to be monitored by the built-in class.

For example, it makes sense for AnimatedSprite to emit a `frame_changed` signal when the frame is changed by playback because that is what is happening in the playback method, and the user is not directly instructing it to change the frame. The `sprite_frames_changed` signal makes sense too, since the built-in SpriteFramesEditor class needs to monitor it.

Conversely, the flipping is only changed by an explicit setter, and Sprite2D/3D `flip` properties don't need to be monitored by any other built-in class. so this signal is meaningless. Since **the `flip` properties are only set by the user**, it is up to the user to emit the signal or call a callback method. In other words, what this PR is trying to do can be implemented in a few lines on the user side.

Saying that a signal is needed in such a case is like saying that a changed signal needs to be emitted for all properties.
